head_neck.label: Carboplatin with radiotherapy

medicines.name: Aprepitant
medicines.dose: 125 mg orally on Day 1; 80 mg orally on Days 2 and 3
medicines.timing: Once daily on each listed day
medicines.note: Check interactions; follow the prescribed plan.

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.note: NCIS permits individual splitting to 8 mg twice daily or reduction to 8 mg once daily. Review QT risk, electrolytes and constipation.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.dose: 12 mg orally on Day 1; 8 mg orally on Days 2, 3 and 4
medicines.timing: Once daily on each listed day
medicines.note: Confirm timing and diabetes/sleep advice. This is the dedicated carboplatin row.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide · duration requires prescription
medicines.dose: 10 mg orally three times daily on subsequent days in the NCIS row
medicines.timing: The source row does not specify an end day or PRN qualifier
medicines.note: Prescriber/pharmacist must specify duration and suitability, including renal function and neurological contraindications. Do not continue indefinitely.

additional_support: This carboplatin regimen has high sickness risk. Take the prescribed prevention and rescue medicines on their written schedule. Call if nausea or vomiting prevents drinking.
Tell the team early if swallowing, appetite, pain or taste changes reduce intake. A dietitian can agree practical food, drink or feeding support with you. Do not wait for substantial weight loss.
Agree a mouth-care plan and tell your dentist about previous or current cancer treatment. Arrange oncology advice before dental procedures, particularly after head and neck radiation.
Ask for speech and language therapy if swallowing or speech is difficult. Use the food textures, exercises and communication support advised for you; a general guide cannot establish safe swallowing.

Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Carboplatin can impair fertility. Do not breastfeed during treatment. The linked Irish product information advises contraception for women during treatment and at least six months afterwards; men should avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least three months afterwards. Confirm the actual product and personal advice.

Continue mouth, swallowing, dental, skin and nutrition care after radiation. Blood tests and hearing or nerve review follow any persisting problem; scans and examinations follow your individual oncology and radiation plan.
NCIS Table 1 allows clinician-selected ondansetron splitting to 8 mg twice daily or reduction to 8 mg once daily according to the individual patient.
Review ondansetron QT risk and other QT-prolonging medicines/electrolytes.
Check dexamethasone interactions, diabetes, sleep and infection effects; aprepitant/steroid interaction is already reflected in the specified row.
Review metoclopramide renal function, neurological contraindications, duration and extrapyramidal risk; do not automatically stack with olanzapine.
AUC reduction below 4 requires an individual prophylaxis review; history of emesis and patient factors may justify continuing stronger protection.
No universal G-CSF, antibiotic, antiviral or acid-suppression prescription is stated by the carboplatin protocol. G-CSF requires individual febrile-neutropenia risk review.
Routine hypersensitivity premedication is usually unnecessary, but antiemetic prophylaxis is still required. Prior allergy/desensitisation is a separate specialist plan.
Use the dedicated carboplatin AUC ≥4 row. It does not include routine olanzapine.
head_neck.prescription_note: Source-based NCIS carboplatin AUC ≥4 draft. Prescriber/pharmacist must individualise, specify metoclopramide duration and authorise before use. Concurrent radiotherapy supportive care follows its separate plan.
head_neck.source_page: NCCP 00261 v7 p4; NCIS antiemetics v8 Table 1 pp4–5

head_neck.label: Nivolumab monotherapy
additional_support: Routine preventive anti-sickness or steroid medicines are not usually needed for this monotherapy. Steroids or hormone replacement may be prescribed for a specific complication; they are not a generic prophylactic prescription.

Carry your immune alert card during and after nivolumab. Tell any clinician that you have received immunotherapy. Do not restart a held treatment or change prescribed steroids or hormone replacement yourself.
Tell the team early if swallowing, appetite, pain or taste changes reduce intake. A dietitian can agree practical food, drink or feeding support with you. Do not wait for substantial weight loss.
Agree a mouth-care plan and tell your dentist about previous or current cancer treatment. Arrange oncology advice before dental procedures, particularly after head and neck radiation.
Ask for speech and language therapy if swallowing or speech is difficult. Use the food textures, exercises and communication support advised for you; a general guide cannot establish safe swallowing.

Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least five months after the final dose. Tell the team promptly about a possible pregnancy. Do not breastfeed without specific advice from the team.

Keep reporting new symptoms after treatment ends. Immune side effects require monitoring for at least five months after the last dose. Steroid tapers, hormone replacement or specialist review may continue longer. Scans and examinations follow your individual response and follow-up plan.
